newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Activists disrupt EU treaty announcement.
newsitem.headline: Activists disrupt EU treaty announcement.

text.p: A small group of environmental protestors disrupted the final press conference of a two-day European Union summit on Wednesday, staging a brief but noisy protest before being dragged away screaming by police.
As soon as Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok announced that a new Treaty of Amsterdam had been agreed after marathon talks, the protestors ran through the auditorium, shouting and screaming.
Complaining about the treaty and its effect on democracy and the environment, two demonstrators unfurled a banner proclaiming "Excluded! Human Rights", while others called out "Reclaim Europe".

"There were about seven of them, and they were arrested afterwards," said a policeman outside the theatre where the conference was being held within the high security complex of the downtown summit site around the Dutch central bank.

Kok, who was accompanied on stage by European Commission President Jacques Santer and other officials, remained calm throughout the incident, and resumed his address after around ten minutes once the protestors had been removed.
